_note: Check registry — the single source of truth for what Citely measures. Analyzers emit a state per check id; _scoring.py turns states into scores. Thresholds live HERE (not in analyzer code) so they are auditable and tunable in one place. 24 checks, 6 per category: engagement sits at exact parity with discoverability, per the rubric's 'across both discoverability and engagement'.

_field_reference.id: Stable identifier. Never reuse or renumber — findings and tests reference it.
_field_reference.category: One of the four scoring categories.
_field_reference.weight: Relative weight WITHIN its category. Weights per category sum to 100.
_field_reference.confidence_class: verified = directly observed fact; heuristic = inference. Inherited by emitted findings as `confidence`.
_field_reference.kind: structural = binary/language-independent, near-zero false-positive risk. statistical = threshold-dependent, biased toward partial/unknown near the boundary.
_field_reference.depends_on: Prerequisite check ids. If a prerequisite FAILS, this check becomes `unknown` (not `fail`) — collapsing correlated findings. Anti-dodge rule: suppression only applies when the failed prerequisite is confidence_class `verified`.
_field_reference.requires_language: true = needs confident, supported page-language detection. Otherwise resolves to `unknown`, never `fail` (prevents mass false positives on non-English sites).
_field_reference.threshold: Measured values compared against these. null = purely structural presence check.
_field_reference.title: Short finding title.
_field_reference.signal: The mechanism being measured (first link of the reasoning chain).
_field_reference.impact: Why it matters for AI ingestion or human retention.
_field_reference.plain_summary: Non-expert phrasing for the report's layer-1 verdict.
_field_reference.remediation: Plain-language fix, used as suggested_action.summary. Lives here so report wording has one source of truth; Phase 7's advisor enriches it with snippets and validation steps.
_field_reference.failure_title: Finding title when the check does NOT pass. `title` states what good looks like, which reads backwards in a finding ('Mobile viewport is declared' when it is missing).
_field_reference.failure_summary: Non-expert phrasing of the PROBLEM, used as the finding's plain_summary.
_field_reference.partial_title: Finding title when the check is PARTIAL rather than failed. Only present where the failure title would be false for a partial (an absolute 'No X' when some X exists); otherwise the failure title covers both and is reused.
_field_reference.partial_summary: Non-expert phrasing of a PARTIAL result. Falls back to failure_summary when absent.

checks.title: Page returns a successful HTTP status
checks.signal: HTTP status of the final URL after redirects
checks.impact: A non-2xx response means no AI crawler can ingest the page at all; every downstream signal is unmeasurable.
checks.plain_summary: AI assistants can load your page.
checks.remediation: Fix the server error so the page returns a successful response. Check hosting logs and any redirect rules for this URL.
checks.failure_title: Page does not load successfully
checks.failure_summary: AI assistants cannot load your page at all.

checks.title: robots.txt permits the AI assistants' crawlers
checks.signal: robots.txt directives evaluated for each major AI crawler user-agent (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, OAI-SearchBot) on the target path
checks.impact: This is the single most direct way to be invisible to AI assistants. A site can be fully crawlable by search engines yet block GPTBot, in which case ChatGPT can never read or cite it. The block is often a CDN or platform default the site owner never consciously chose.
checks.plain_summary: The AI assistants' crawlers are allowed to read your site.
checks._note: Deliberately evaluated for the AI crawlers, NOT for CitelyAuditBot. Whether OUR bot may fetch is an operational gate handled by the orchestrator (stop + partial_reason 'blocked'), not a scored check — nobody blocks an unknown auditor UA, so scoring that would pass on every site and miss real AI-crawler blocks.
checks.remediation: Edit robots.txt to allow the AI assistants' crawlers. Remove or narrow the Disallow rules for the user-agents listed in the evidence.
checks.failure_title: robots.txt blocks the AI assistants' crawlers
checks.failure_summary: Your robots.txt is telling AI assistants to stay out.

checks.title: Page is not marked noindex
checks.signal: meta name=robots content and the X-Robots-Tag response header
checks.impact: A noindex directive tells engines not to retain the page, so its facts never enter the index AI systems draw on.
checks.plain_summary: Your page is not telling search engines to ignore it.
checks.remediation: Remove the noindex directive from the page's meta robots tag or from the X-Robots-Tag response header.
checks.failure_title: Page is marked noindex
checks.failure_summary: Your page is telling search engines to ignore it.

threshold._note: This check measures JS-DEPENDENCE, not thinness. Above min_visible_chars_raw the page passes outright. Below it, we only fail when there is positive evidence that JavaScript is responsible (empty mount node, framework markers, or a large render gain) or when the page is below empty_floor_chars (50) and therefore effectively blank. The floor is deliberately low: a small-but-real page (a local business homepage of ~80 characters) is thin, not JavaScript-dependent, and flagging it here would be a false positive. A short but genuinely server-rendered page is NOT a rendering defect — sparse content is judged by the information-density check instead.

checks.title: Meaningful content exists without JavaScript
checks.signal: Visible text length in the raw (pre-JavaScript) HTML response
checks.impact: Crawlers that do not execute JavaScript see an empty shell. Facts that only appear after hydration are invisible to them, so nothing is quotable or citable.
checks.plain_summary: Your content is in the page itself, not built later by the browser.
checks.remediation: Server-render or pre-render the page so its key facts are present in the initial HTML, before any JavaScript runs.
checks.failure_title: Content only appears after JavaScript runs
checks.failure_summary: AI assistants that do not run JavaScript see an empty page.

checks.title: Semantic HTML landmarks present
checks.signal: Presence of main/article/header/nav landmarks delimiting content from chrome
checks.impact: Semantic structure tells extractors which text is primary content versus navigation and boilerplate.
checks.plain_summary: Your page structure marks out what the main content is.
checks.remediation: Wrap the primary content in a <main> or <article> element, so extractors can tell content from navigation and boilerplate.
checks.failure_title: Semantic HTML landmarks are missing
checks.failure_summary: Nothing marks out which part of the page is the main content.
checks.partial_summary: Your page structure only partly marks out the main content.
checks._h1_note: Heading structure is deliberately NOT graded here. `content.heading_hierarchy` owns it and already requires exactly one h1; grading it in both places charged a missing h1 twice, in two different categories, which no suppression edge could catch.

threshold._note: An image smaller than min_fact_image_px cannot hold a readable fact, and a filename that is a build fingerprint (content hash, UUID, bare row id, URL-encoded path) is not evidence of one. Matching any digit flagged 79 of 108 images on dev.to, 59 of them 18x18 reaction icons.

checks.title: Key facts are not locked inside images
checks.signal: Ratio of images carrying apparent factual content (numbers, claims) with no equivalent text or alt
checks.impact: Text baked into images, SVG or canvas cannot be parsed into embeddings, so those facts are unavailable for citation even though a human can read them.
checks.plain_summary: Your important facts are written as text, not trapped in pictures.
checks.remediation: Repeat any facts shown inside images as real text, or add alt text carrying the same numbers and claims.
checks.failure_title: Key facts are locked inside images
checks.failure_summary: Some of your facts exist only as pictures, so AI cannot read them.
checks.partial_title: Some facts are locked inside images
checks.partial_summary: A few of your facts exist only as pictures.

checks.title: Descriptive page title
checks.signal: Length and presence of the document title element
checks.impact: The title is the strongest single hint an AI summarizer uses to decide what a page is about.
checks.plain_summary: Your page title clearly says what the page is.
checks.remediation: Write a page title of roughly 15-70 characters that names the page and what it offers.
checks.failure_title: Page title is missing or unhelpful
checks.failure_summary: Your page title does not clearly say what the page is.
checks.partial_title: Page title is the wrong length
checks.partial_summary: Your page title exists but is too short or too long to work well.

checks.title: Meta description present and usable
checks.signal: Presence and length of meta name=description
checks.impact: Provides a ready-made summary that answer engines frequently reuse verbatim.
checks.plain_summary: Your page has a short summary engines can reuse.
checks.remediation: Add a meta description of roughly 50-160 characters summarising the page in one sentence an answer engine could reuse verbatim.
checks.failure_title: Meta description is missing or the wrong length
checks.failure_summary: There is no short summary for answer engines to reuse.
checks.partial_title: Meta description is the wrong length
checks.partial_summary: You have a summary, but its length limits how well engines can reuse it.

checks.title: Logical heading hierarchy
checks.signal: Heading level sequence (h1 to h6) checked for skipped levels and multiple h1s
checks.impact: Headings define the document outline summarizers use to decide which sections survive condensation.
checks.plain_summary: Your headings are in a sensible order.
checks.remediation: Use exactly one <h1> and step heading levels one at a time (h1 then h2, never h1 then h4).
checks.failure_title: Heading structure is inconsistent
checks.failure_summary: Your headings are not in a sensible order.
checks.partial_summary: Your headings are mostly sensible but skip levels or repeat the top level.

threshold._note: A page with no lists or tables is only failed when it is long enough that structure would clearly help; short prose pages get `partial`, not `fail`.

checks.title: Facts presented in scannable blocks
checks.signal: Presence of lists, tables or definition lists carrying factual content
checks.impact: Structured blocks are extracted far more reliably than the same facts buried in prose paragraphs.
checks.plain_summary: Key details appear in lists or tables, not only in paragraphs.
checks.remediation: Move key facts out of prose into a list, table or definition list, which are extracted far more reliably than paragraphs.
checks.failure_title: Facts are buried in prose
checks.failure_summary: Key details are locked in paragraphs instead of lists or tables.
checks.partial_summary: Most of your key details sit in paragraphs rather than lists or tables.

threshold._language: en — applied ONLY when the page declares a supported language (requires_language=true); otherwise the check is `unknown`, never `fail`.

checks.title: Self-contained, quotable factual statements
checks.signal: Count of sentences that state a complete fact without needing surrounding context
checks.impact: Retrieval systems cite sentences that stand alone. Statements that depend on the previous paragraph get dropped.
checks.plain_summary: Your page makes clear standalone statements an AI can quote.
checks.remediation: Rewrite key claims as complete standalone sentences that name the subject, so each still makes sense when quoted on its own.
checks.failure_title: Few statements can stand alone as quotes
checks.failure_summary: Your sentences do not make sense when quoted on their own.
checks.partial_title: Few statements stand alone as quotes
checks.partial_summary: Only a little of your text makes sense when quoted on its own.

checks.title: Information density survives summarization
checks.signal: Ratio of concrete factual sentences to total sentences, weighted by page length
checks.impact: When a summarizer condenses a long page, low-density facts surrounded by filler are the first thing discarded.
checks.plain_summary: Your key facts are not diluted by filler text.
checks.remediation: Replace vague marketing phrasing with concrete specifics — numbers, dates, named capabilities — so the facts survive summarising.
checks.failure_title: Facts are diluted by filler
checks.failure_summary: Your key facts are surrounded by too much vague wording.
checks.partial_summary: Your key facts compete with a fair amount of vague wording.

checks.title: Structured data is present
checks.signal: Presence of parseable JSON-LD, microdata or RDFa
checks.impact: Without structured data an AI must infer identity from prose, which is where mistaken-identity and hallucination begin.
checks.plain_summary: Your page includes machine-readable information about itself.
checks.remediation: Add a JSON-LD block describing this page. Open Graph tags are not a substitute: they drive social previews and carry no schema.org type, so a machine still cannot tell what kind of thing this page is about.
checks.failure_title: No structured data on the page
checks.failure_summary: Your page has no machine-readable description of what it is about.
checks.partial_title: Structured data uses the older format
checks.partial_summary: Your page has microdata but no JSON-LD, which is the format answer engines read most reliably.

checks.title: An organization or person entity is declared
checks.signal: A schema.org entity of an accepted identity type in the structured data graph
checks.impact: This is the anchor that tells an AI who the page is about. Without it the brand has no declared identity to attach facts to.
checks.plain_summary: Your page states who you are in a way machines understand.
checks.remediation: Add a JSON-LD Organization (or Person) entry that names who this site is about.
checks.failure_title: No organization or person entity declared
checks.failure_summary: Your page never states who it is about in a way machines understand.
checks.partial_summary: Your page names who it is, but not in a form machines can corroborate.

checks.title: sameAs cross-references present
checks.signal: sameAs property on the declared entity
checks.impact: sameAs links let an AI corroborate your identity across the web instead of guessing between similarly named businesses.
checks.plain_summary: You link out to your other official profiles.
checks.remediation: Add sameAs links from your Organization entry to the profiles and listings you already link to, such as your Google Business, Facebook or LinkedIn page. If you have no structured data yet, rel="me" on those links is a valid alternative.
checks.failure_title: Your identity is not linked to anything else
checks.failure_summary: Nothing on the page connects you to your profiles or listings elsewhere on the web.
checks.partial_title: Your profiles are linked but not declared
checks.partial_summary: You link to your own profiles, but not in a way that states they are you.

checks.title: At least one sameAs points to an authority node
checks.signal: sameAs targets matched against known authority domains
checks.impact: Corroboration needs a record the brand does not control. Links only to your own accounts leave an AI unable to tell you apart from a similarly named business.
checks.plain_summary: At least one of your links points somewhere authoritative.
checks.remediation: Link to at least one record somebody else maintains. A Google Business Profile, a Yelp or industry-directory listing, or a companies-registry entry all work; Wikidata or Wikipedia are the strongest but are not required.
checks.failure_title: Your identity is not anchored to any outside record
checks.failure_summary: Nothing you link to is a record maintained by someone other than you.
checks.partial_title: Your identity is anchored only to your own profiles
checks.partial_summary: You link to accounts you control, which cannot settle which business you are.

checks.title: Open Graph identity tags present
checks.signal: Presence of core og: properties
checks.impact: Open Graph is a widely consumed secondary identity signal and a fallback when JSON-LD is absent or malformed.
checks.plain_summary: Your page has social/preview tags describing it.
checks.remediation: Add the core Open Graph tags (og:title, og:type, og:url) to the page head.
checks.failure_title: Open Graph identity tags missing
checks.failure_summary: Your page lacks the social/preview tags that describe it.
checks.partial_title: Open Graph identity tags are incomplete
checks.partial_summary: You have some social/preview tags, but not all the core ones.

checks.title: Entity naming is internally consistent
checks.signal: Entity name compared across JSON-LD blocks, Open Graph site name and the document title
checks.impact: Contradictory names across blocks actively teach an AI the wrong association and are worse than no data at all.
checks.plain_summary: Your brand name is stated the same way everywhere on the page.
checks.remediation: State one exact spelling of your name in your JSON-LD entry, in og:site_name and in the page title, so the three agree.
checks.failure_title: Entity naming is inconsistent
checks.failure_summary: Your brand name is written differently in different places.
checks.partial_title: Your name is stated, but nothing confirms it
checks.partial_summary: Your brand name appears in only one place, so nothing corroborates it.

threshold._proxy_note: Tier A uses real pixel offsets. Tier B falls back to a DOM-order proxy budgeted in VISIBLE TEXT, not markup: a raw markup slice is consumed by inline <svg>, critical-CSS <style> blocks and mega-menu markup long before it reaches the content. On python.org the first 16,151 characters of <body> hold 11,414 characters of tags and 1,345 of text. Chrome (<nav>, <header>, dialogs) is charged at chrome_text_weight per character up to chrome_text_cap, because a collapsed menu occupies one bar on screen however many links it holds; past that allowance its text costs full price, so wrapping a page in <nav> buys nothing. Verdicts from this path are labelled heuristic.

checks.title: A heading appears in the first viewport
checks.signal: Presence of an h1 or hero heading within the first viewport height
checks.impact: A visitor arriving from an AI answer has seconds to confirm they landed in the right place. No heading means no confirmation.
checks.plain_summary: Visitors see a clear headline as soon as they land.
checks.remediation: Put a clear headline at the top of the page so arriving visitors immediately see what it is.
checks.failure_title: No heading in the first viewport
checks.failure_summary: Visitors do not see a clear headline when they land.

threshold._proxy_note: Tier A uses real pixel offsets. Tier B falls back to a DOM-order proxy budgeted in VISIBLE TEXT, not markup: a raw markup slice is consumed by inline <svg>, critical-CSS <style> blocks and mega-menu markup long before it reaches the content. On python.org the first 16,151 characters of <body> hold 11,414 characters of tags and 1,345 of text. Chrome (<nav>, <header>, dialogs) is charged at chrome_text_weight per character up to chrome_text_cap, because a collapsed menu occupies one bar on screen however many links it holds; past that allowance its text costs full price, so wrapping a page in <nav> buys nothing. Verdicts from this path are labelled heuristic.

checks.title: A primary action is available above the fold
checks.signal: An anchor or button element positioned within the first viewport
checks.impact: Without an obvious next step, AI-referred visitors read once and leave rather than converting.
checks.plain_summary: There is something obvious to click when visitors arrive.
checks.remediation: Place a clear link or button above the fold giving arriving visitors an obvious next step.
checks.failure_title: No clear action above the fold
checks.failure_summary: There is nothing obvious to click when visitors arrive.

threshold._note: Overlay coverage comes from Tier-A geometry (fixed/sticky elements). A page already flagged as a consent wall or bot challenge fails here too.

checks.title: First-paint content is not obstructed
checks.signal: Full-viewport overlays, modals or consent interstitials covering initial content
checks.impact: An interstitial covering the first screen hides the very answer the visitor arrived for.
checks.plain_summary: No popup covers your content the moment visitors arrive.
checks.remediation: Stop the overlay or consent banner covering the first screen — make it smaller, or dismissible without hiding the content behind it.
checks.failure_title: Content is obstructed on arrival
checks.failure_summary: Something covers your content the moment visitors arrive.

checks.title: Mobile viewport is declared
checks.signal: Presence of meta name=viewport
checks.impact: Most AI-referred traffic is mobile. Without a viewport declaration the page renders unusably small.
checks.plain_summary: Your page is set up to display properly on phones.
checks.remediation: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> so the page renders correctly on phones, where most AI-referred traffic arrives.
checks.failure_title: Mobile viewport is not declared
checks.failure_summary: Your page is not set up to display properly on phones.

threshold._language: en — gated by requires_language. A non-English hero section must never be judged with English vocabulary.
threshold._min_text_note: Below this much above-the-fold text there is nothing that could constitute a value proposition, so the check fails outright rather than scoring an incidental keyword match (a 'Loading...' shell was matching the offering-noun 'app').
threshold._proxy_note: Tier A uses real pixel offsets. Tier B falls back to a DOM-order proxy budgeted in VISIBLE TEXT, not markup: a raw markup slice is consumed by inline <svg>, critical-CSS <style> blocks and mega-menu markup long before it reaches the content. On python.org the first 16,151 characters of <body> hold 11,414 characters of tags and 1,345 of text. Chrome (<nav>, <header>, dialogs) is charged at chrome_text_weight per character up to chrome_text_cap, because a collapsed menu occupies one bar on screen however many links it holds; past that allowance its text costs full price, so wrapping a page in <nav> buys nothing. Verdicts from this path are labelled heuristic.
threshold._vocabulary_note: action_verbs and offering_nouns are POSITIVE EVIDENCE ONLY, never a requirement — PLAN §8: 'no hardcoded allowlists … used only as positive evidence, never as a requirement'. Gating on them failed 'Emergency lock repair across Leeds' at high severity while passing example.com, which has no value proposition at all: an 18-noun list cannot hold the open web's product categories, exactly as a five-name type allowlist could not hold schema.org's ~200 LocalBusiness subtypes (fixed 2026-09-10). Specificity is now the primary signal: a concrete anchor is a figure with a unit or a proper noun. vague_markers are the mirror image and are used ONLY to subtract — a marker missing from the list can never cause a failure, which is what makes an open-ended list safe here and unsafe as a gate.

checks.title: A value proposition is stated above the fold
checks.signal: Above-the-fold text evaluated for an action plus an offering
checks.impact: Visitors who cannot tell what you do within the first screen bounce regardless of how accurate the AI citation was.
checks.plain_summary: Visitors can tell what you offer without scrolling.
checks.remediation: State plainly in the headline area what you do and who it is for, so a visitor from an AI answer can confirm within seconds that they are in the right place.
checks.failure_title: No clear value proposition above the fold
checks.failure_summary: Visitors cannot tell what you offer without scrolling.
checks.partial_summary: Visitors get a hint of what you offer, but not a clear statement.

threshold._note: Requires a real computed font size from a Tier-A render. Without geometry this resolves to `unknown` — guessing from inline styles would be unreliable.

checks.title: Body text is legible
checks.signal: Computed or declared body font size
checks.impact: Text below roughly 14px is difficult to read on mobile, increasing bounce for AI-referred visitors.
checks.plain_summary: Your body text is big enough to read comfortably.
checks.remediation: Increase body text to at least 14px so it is comfortable to read on a phone.
checks.failure_title: Body text is too small
checks.failure_summary: Your body text is smaller than is comfortable to read.

categories._note: Plain-language verdicts for PLAN.md §9 layer 1 — one sentence per category, chosen by score band, with no undefined jargon. They live here because report wording lives ONCE in this file and is applied by the orchestrator, which is what stops it drifting. A band is selected by the FIRST entry whose `min` the score meets, so bands are ordered high to low. `unmeasured` is used when the category has no score at all, or when its coverage is below the floor — a sentence about a score built on a minority of the evidence would read as a verdict on the site, which it is not.

ai_discoverability.label: Getting found and read
ai_discoverability.question: Can an AI assistant reach your page and read what is on it?

bands.verdict: AI assistants can reach your page and read what is on it.
AI assistants can reach your page, but part of what it says is hard for them to read.
AI assistants cannot reliably read your page, so your facts may never reach them.

ai_discoverability.unmeasured: We could not check whether AI assistants can read your page.

ai_comprehension.label: Being understood and quoted
ai_comprehension.question: Can an assistant lift a clear fact out of your page and quote it?

bands.verdict: Your page states its facts clearly enough to be quoted.
Your page can be read, but its key facts are hard to lift out and quote.
Your page does not state its facts in a form an assistant can quote.

ai_comprehension.unmeasured: We could not check how quotable your page's facts are.

entity_trust.label: Being recognised as you
entity_trust.question: Can a machine tell which business this is, and confirm it somewhere else?

bands.verdict: Your page says clearly who you are and points to other places that confirm it.
Your page gives some sense of who you are, but not enough to tell you apart from a similarly named business.
Nothing on your page tells a machine which business this is.

entity_trust.unmeasured: We could not check whether your page says who you are.

human_orientation.label: Keeping the visitor
human_orientation.question: Can someone arriving from an AI answer tell they are in the right place?

bands.verdict: A visitor arriving from an AI answer can immediately tell what you do.
A visitor arriving from an AI answer has to work to tell what you do.
A visitor arriving from an AI answer cannot tell what you do, and is likely to leave.

human_orientation.unmeasured: We could not check what a visitor sees when they arrive.

bands.verdict: Your site is in good shape for AI assistants to find, read and cite.
AI assistants can work with your site, but several things are holding back how often it gets cited.
AI assistants will struggle to find, read or cite your site.

overall.unmeasured: We could not measure enough of your site to give it a score.
overall.low_coverage_caveat: This score comes from fewer than half of the checks, because most of the page could not be measured. Treat it as provisional and read what could not be checked before acting on the number.

reasons._note: Plain-language translations of the scoring engine's reason codes, for §9 layers 1 and 2 where undefined jargon is not allowed. 'suppressed_by_failed_prerequisite' is accurate and means nothing to a reader, so where a blocking check is known the report names THAT instead, in its own words.
reasons.suppressed_by_failed_prerequisite: these checks could not be judged until something they depend on is fixed first
reasons.language_unsupported_or_undetected: the page's language could not be confirmed, so checks that read wording were skipped rather than guessed
reasons.not_measured: no result came back for these checks
reasons.blocked_before_fetch: the page could not be fetched, so nothing on it could be measured
